_comment: The authoritative identity of every RECOG-C1 measurement artifact, in a form a
script can read. It exists because a hash computed FROM the artifact under
suspicion proves only that the artifact agrees with itself: the deploy step used
to hash the very plan it was about to push and compile that value into the APK,
so a stale or hand-edited plan supplied both sides of the equality and passed
every check on both ends perfectly.
The reference must therefore be independent of the artifact. recog_c1_deploy.ps1
reads this file out of the COMMITTED tree (git show HEAD:...), never from the
working copy, so editing it locally changes nothing. Editing it for real means
committing it, which puts it in the history where a reviewer can see it.
Hashes are of the newline-normalised bytes. Git checks these files out as CRLF on
the machine that produced them while the generators write LF, so the raw
working-tree hash is not stable across checkouts and would fail for the wrong
reason. See RECOG_C1_GT_FREEZE_2026-09-05.md, which records both forms.
